sections.label: Growth in registered professional engineers
sections.summary: Registered PEs rose 20% to around 3,900, and licensed professional engineering service entities grew from 76 to over 200.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Since then, the number of registered PEs has increased by 20% to around 3,900 today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The number of licensed entities providing professional engineering services has grown to two and a half times, from 76 to over 200.

sections.label: Higher maximum financial penalties
sections.summary: Clause 18(b) increases maximum financial penalties to S$100,000 for serious infringements with public safety implications.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 18(b) will now increase maximum financial penalties to S$100,000 for serious infringements with public safety implications.

sections.label: ASEAN MRA and Chartered PEs
sections.summary: The MRA framework is expected to be fully in place in all ASEAN countries by year end, letting qualifying Singapore-registered PEs be recognised as ACPEs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The MRA framework is expected to be fully in place in all ASEAN countries by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: With these amendments, Singapore-registered PEs who meet the requirements specified in the MRA can be recognised as ASEAN Chartered PEs (ACPEs).

sections.label: Specialist PEs as consultants
sections.summary: The first proposal allows professional engineering companies to engage specialist PEs as consultants to take on more complex projects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The first proposal will allow professional engineering companies to engage specialist PEs as consultants so that they can take on more complex projects.

sections.label: Builders directly employing PEs
sections.summary: The second proposal, in clause 9(d), allows builders to directly employ PEs for low-risk professional engineering works on their own projects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The second proposal, which is in clause 9(d), will allow builders to directly employ PEs to undertake low-risk professional engineering works pertaining to their own projects.

sections.label: Effect of proposed amendments
sections.summary: The proposed amendments will raise standards, help PEs capture overseas opportunities, and provide a more pro-enterprise environment for local firms and contractors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Taken together, the proposed amendments will raise standards, help our PEs capture overseas opportunities, and provide a more pro-enterprise environment for local professional engineering firms and contractors.

sections.label: Expanding Professional Engineers Board functions
sections.summary: The speaker serves on the PEB and welcomes the Bill expanding the Board's functions to promote professional engineering development in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am also currently serving on the PEB.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am pleased that the Bill will expand the functions of the Board to allow it to promote the development of Professional Engineering in Singapore.

sections.label: Part-time specialised engineering courses
sections.summary: The speaker hopes higher learning institutions offer more specialised part-time courses, possibly with engineering bodies and SkillsFuture funding, module by module.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Another point I would like to make is that in the interest of upskilling, I hope the institutions of higher learning and others look into more specialised courses on a part-time basis.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It will be even better if they can collaborate with the various engineering bodies on this, and SkillsFuture fund can be used to pursue those specialised courses module by module.

sections.label: More engineering scholarships proposed
sections.summary: The speaker says Government should return to giving more scholarships to engineering students, as done in early nation-building years, to reverse the trend.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In order to reverse this trend, the Government should go back to the old practice of giving more scholarships to engineering students, just like what we did in the early years of our nation-building.

sections.label: Engineers needed for Smart Nation
sections.summary: The speaker states that without engineers, Singapore will not be able to build a Smart Nation.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, without engineers, we will not be able to build a Smart Nation.

sections.label: PEB powers to censure firms
sections.summary: The Bill gives PEB power and discretion to censure licensed firms providing PE services, and the speaker asks about warning letters, targets and public recourse.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: One, under the current practice, PEB can only revoke the licence or impose a penalty up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: With changes in the Bill, PEB will have the power and discretion to censure licensed firms providing PE services.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The question is (a) under what circumstances, for example, how many warning letters would PEB issue before revoking the licence; (b) would the warning letters be issued against PEs or the companies that they work for; (c) when PEs undertake private contractual jobs and disputes arise, is the general public able to seek advice and recourse through PEB?

sections.label: Removing three-year stand-down for PEs
sections.summary: The speaker calls it a positive move to remove the three-year stand-down for deregistered PEs, especially those deregistered for minor violations like no contact address.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Three, it is a positive move to remove the need for a three-year stand-down for deregistered PEs, especially those who were deregistered under current rules for minor violations, for example, no contact address provided in Singapore.

sections.label: Amendments to Engineers Act sections
sections.summary: The amendments allow undergraduates to register as PEs and re-enact section 35 with new section 35A to encourage whistleblowing and prevent scapegoating.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, the rationale to amend section 15(2), as the explanation notes point out, is to allow an undergraduate to be registered as a PE.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Three, the re-enactment of section 35 and the new section 35A provides the necessary safeguards to encourage whistleblowing and eliminate any scapegoating behaviour that may be adopted by the management.

sections.label: Authorising foreign PEs processes
sections.summary: The MP asks what processes and criteria the Board will use to authorise foreign PEs and whether a ratio for working with Registered PEs will be established.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what are the processes and criteria the Board will use for authorising foreign PEs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I do understand that the Registered Foreign PE must work with a Registered PE but will there an established ratio for this?

sections.label: Chemical engineering prescribed branch
sections.summary: Chemical engineering was introduced as a prescribed branch of professional engineering last November based on MOM's assessment that Chemical PEs were needed for Major Hazard Installations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For example, chemical engineering was just introduced as a prescribed branch of professional engineering last November.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The decision was based on the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) assessment that Chemical PEs were needed to ensure the safety of Major Hazard Installations, such as chemical plants.

sections.label: Four years work experience
sections.summary: Applicants must have at least four years of practical work experience before attending the professional interview.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For instance, applicants must have at least four years of practical work experience before they can attend the professional interview.

sections.label: One-year validity if approved
sections.summary: If approved, this will be valid for one year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If approved, this will be valid for one year.

sections.label: Ratios for RFPE collaboration
sections.summary: The Board will look at whether sensible ratios can be put in place, in rules, practice directions or guidelines, for how many RFPEs a Singapore PE can collaborate with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Board will also be looking at whether sensible ratios can be put in place, whether in rules, practice directions or guidelines, of how many RFPEs that a Singapore PE can collaborate with.

sections.label: Singaporeans among professional engineers
sections.summary: Singaporeans make up almost 80% of the 3,900 PEs, a proportion steady for 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Of the 3,900 PEs that we have today, Singaporeans make up almost 80%, and this proportion has held steady for the last 10 years.

sections.label: Scholarships given out this year
sections.summary: Eight of these scholarships were given out this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Eight of these scholarships were given out this year.

sections.label: Monetary award for successful applicants
sections.summary: Successful applicants receive a S$5,000 monetary award for out-of-pocket study expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Successful applicants will receive a monetary award of S$5,000 which can be used to defray out-of-pocket expenses associated with their study.

sections.label: Bill on professional engineering standards
sections.summary: The Bill aims to raise PE standards, enhance overseas opportunities and provide a more pro-enterprise environment for local engineering firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In summary, we place great importance on developing our engineering profession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I am confident that this Bill, which will help to raise the standards of PEs, enhance their access to overseas opportunities and provide a more pro-enterprise environment for local professional engineering firms, is a step in the right direction.
